market_context: United States; current fat composition and labeling
title: Butter vs Margarine: Which Has the Better Fat Profile Today?

seo.title: Butter vs Margarine: Which Is Better Today?
seo.meta_description: Modern soft margarines are often lower in saturated fat and no longer resemble older partially hydrogenated products. Compare the actual label because formulas vary.
seo.search_intent: Compare current butter and margarine fat profiles without relying on outdated assumptions about trans fat.

excerpt: A soft margarine made mostly from unsaturated vegetable oils is usually lower in saturated fat than butter. Older comparisons based on heavily partially hydrogenated margarines do not describe many products sold today, so the specific label matters.
content_html:
Margarine's reputation was shaped by an older generation of products made with partially hydrogenated oils. The market changed. A modern soft spread built around unsaturated oils can have a more favorable fat profile than butter.

Butter remains high in saturated fat

Butter contains about 51 grams of saturated fat per 100 grams, or roughly 7 grams per tablespoon. Margarine has no single number because formulas differ: tub spreads, sticks, and light products can be quite different.

Soft spreads based on canola, soybean, or sunflower oils are often substantially lower in saturated fat. Firmer products made with more tropical fat may be closer to butter.

Trans fat changed the historical comparison

Partially hydrogenated oils were a major source of industrial trans fat. FDA removed partially hydrogenated oils from the list of ingredients generally recognized as safe, and U.S. products have been reformulated. That makes decades-old margarine comparisons poor guides to a current supermarket shelf.

Use the label, not the category name

Compare saturated fat for the same serving and look for unsaturated oils near the top of the ingredient list. If you prefer butter's flavor, portion size still matters. “Margarine” is not automatically better; a well-formulated soft spread usually is the option that changes the fat profile most.

faq.question: Does margarine still contain trans fat?
faq.answer: Most U.S. products no longer use partially hydrogenated oils, the former major source of industrial trans fat. Always check the current label.

faq.question: Is butter better because it is less processed?
faq.answer: Processing level does not erase butter's high saturated-fat content. The relevant comparison depends on the dietary goal.

faq.question: What should I look for in margarine?
faq.answer: Choose a soft spread based mainly on unsaturated oils and compare saturated fat per serving.
